title: Epic: Full-Text Search
description:
Implement super-performant full-text 'search as you type' across all corpus documents.

## Context & Background

Current state:
- Basic search exists but ONLY for transcript sections (236 segments)
- Runtime parsing (no pre-built index) — slow
- No search across distillations, quote bank, or metaprompts
- Missing: debouncing, highlighting, scope filtering

The corpus is ~589KB total (~68k words) across 7 documents. This is ideal for CLIENT-SIDE search — no server round-trips needed.

## User Value

**Primary users**: Researchers looking for specific Brenner quotes, concepts, or passages
**Key scenarios**:
1. 'What did Brenner say about C. elegans?'
2. 'Find all mentions of exclusion testing'
3. 'Compare how different distillations discuss level-splitting'
4. Quick quote lookup for citations

## Goals

1. **Instant Results**: <50ms response time for any query
2. **Search as You Type**: Results update as user types (with debouncing)
3. **Full Corpus Coverage**: Search all documents, not just transcript
4. **Scope Filtering**: Option to search all docs OR just original transcripts
5. **Context Snippets**: Show matching text with surrounding context
6. **Highlighting**: Matched terms highlighted in results
7. **Keyboard Navigation**: Power users can navigate entirely via keyboard

## Anti-Goals

- NOT implementing server-side search (corpus is small enough for client-side)
- NOT adding fuzzy/semantic search (exact matching is fine for v1)
- NOT building advanced query syntax (simple keyword search)

## Technical Approach

**Recommended: FlexSearch** (lightweight, fast, supports partial matching)
- Build index at build time (not runtime)
- Include index in client bundle (~50-100KB compressed for this corpus)
- Use debounced input (150-200ms)
- Virtualize long result lists

Alternative considered: MiniSearch (smaller bundle, similar performance)

## Success Metrics

- Search response time < 50ms for any query
- Index size < 150KB compressed
- Zero perceived latency on type
- Works offline (index is client-side)

## Technical Considerations

- Integration with existing Command Palette (⌘K)
- May extend or replace current transcript-only search
- Index needs to be rebuilt when corpus changes
- Consider lazy-loading index for faster initial page load
close_reason: All 7 epic goals met: <50ms search, search-as-you-type, full corpus coverage, scope filtering, context snippets, highlighting, keyboard nav. P2 feature x53 (post-navigation enhancements) can be separate follow-up.

## Keep Users Engaged Across Async Work

Research doesn't happen in one sitting. Users set up predictions, await evidence, dispatch agents. They need to know when things happen.

### Notification Types

1. **Agent Completion**
   - "Devil's Advocate has reviewed your hypothesis"
   - "Experiment Designer suggests 3 test modifications"

2. **Prediction Deadline**

3. **Evidence Ready**

   - "View how your prediction compared to outcome"

4. **Session Inactive**
   - "You haven't worked on [hypothesis] in 7 days"

5. **Milestone Reached**
   - "Congratulations! First hypothesis falsified"
   - "Your calibration improved by 10%"

### Delivery Channels
- **In-app**: Badge on session, notification center
- **Browser**: Push notifications (if permitted)
- **Email**: Digest of recent activity (opt-in)

- Which notifications to receive
- How often (real-time, daily digest, never)
- Do not disturb hours

### Implementation

title: Content: Define Extended Brenner Vocabulary (17 terms)
description:
# Extended Brenner Vocabulary Glossary Entries

## Goal
Write glossary entries for specialized Brenner terminology from the distillations.

## Terms to Define

### From the distillations:
1. **abundance-trick**: Bypass purification by choosing systems where target dominates (50-70% of synthesis)
2. **dimensional-reduction**: Collapse 3D physical problems into 1D informational problems
3. **dont-worry-hypothesis**: Assume required mechanisms exist; proceed with theory development
4. **forbidden-pattern**: Observation that cannot occur if hypothesis is true
5. **gedanken-organism**: The reconstruction standard - could you compute the animal from DNA alone?
6. **generative-grammar**: Production rules that generate phenomena; biology as computation
7. **house-of-cards**: Theory with interlocking constraints; p^N becomes tiny when N is large
8. **imprisoned-imagination**: Staying within physical/scale constraints
9. **machine-language**: Operational vocabulary the system actually uses (cells, not gradients)
10. **materialization**: Translating theory to "what would I see if true?"
11. **occams-broom**: The junk swept under the carpet to keep a theory tidy
12. **out-of-phase**: Misaligned with scientific fashion; half a wavelength ahead/behind
13. **productive-ignorance**: Fresh eyes unconstrained by expert priors
14. **seven-cycle-log-paper**: Test for qualitative differences visible "across the room"
15. **topological-proof**: Deducing structure from invariants rather than molecular details
16. **chastity-vs-impotence**: Same outcome, fundamentally different causal reasons

### Additional terms:
17. **brenner-crick-gan**: The conversational approach to hypothesis refinement

## Writing Guidelines
- Many terms are colorful/metaphorical - preserve the flavor
- Ground in transcript examples where possible
- Connect to broader Brenner methodology

## Deliverable
Add entries to `apps/web/src/lib/jargon.ts` under "brenner" category.

title: Tutorial Landing Page: Path Selector & Layout
description:
# Purpose

Create the tutorial landing page at /tutorial that helps users choose the right path for their skill level and goals. This is the "fork in the road" that makes the tutorial accessible to everyone from beginners to power users.

---

# Background & Rationale

## Why a Path Selector?

Different users have different:
- **Goals**: "I want to try this" vs "I want to run multi-agent sessions"
- **Prerequisites**: "I have terminal basics" vs "I have Claude Code + ntm"
- **Time**: "I have 30 minutes" vs "I have 2 hours"

A path selector lets users self-identify and skip irrelevant content.

## UX Inspiration

The ACFS wizard starts with OS selection — a simple choice that gates the rest of the experience. Our equivalent is path selection:
- Quick Start: For most users, lowest barrier
- Agent-Assisted: For power users with AI coding agents
- Multi-Agent: For advanced practitioners

---

# Deliverables

## 1. Tutorial Landing Page
**File**: app/tutorial/page.tsx

**Layout**:
\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  [Hero Section]                                 │
│  "Apply the Brenner Method to Your Research"   │
│  Brief intro paragraph                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  [Path Selection Cards - 3 column grid]         │
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐        │
│  │ Quick    │ │ Agent-   │ │ Multi-   │        │
│  │ Start    │ │ Assisted │ │ Agent    │        │
│  │ ~30 min  │ │ ~45 min  │ │ ~2 hours │        │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  [FAQ Section - Collapsible]                    │
│  "Which path is right for me?"                  │
│  "What if I get stuck?"                         │
│  "Can I switch paths?"                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

**Content**:
- Hero: "Apply the Brenner Method to Your Research"
- Subhead: "Three learning paths from quick start to multi-agent orchestration"
- Path cards with full details (use TutorialPathCard component)
- FAQ section for common questions

---

## 2. Tutorial Layout
**File**: app/tutorial/layout.tsx

**Functionality**:
- Shared layout for all tutorial pages
- Progress sidebar on desktop (left side)
- Mobile-friendly header with progress indicator
- Back to tutorial home link
- Consistent padding and max-width

**Props/Context**:
\`\`\`typescript
// Context for child pages
interface TutorialContext {
  currentPath: TutorialPath | null;
  currentStep: number;
  totalSteps: number;
  completedSteps: number[];
  markStepComplete: (step: number) => void;
}
\`\`\`

**State Persistence**:
- Store progress in localStorage per path
- Allow resuming where user left off
- Clear progress button in settings

---

## 3. Path Landing Pages
**Files**:
- app/tutorial/quick-start/page.tsx
- app/tutorial/agent-assisted/page.tsx
- app/tutorial/multi-agent/page.tsx

**Content**:
- Path-specific introduction
- Prerequisites checklist (interactive checkboxes)
- "Start Step 1" CTA
- Time estimate breakdown per step
- Link back to path selector

---

# Design Specifications

## Path Cards

**Quick Start (Primary accent)**:
\`\`\`
Icon: 🚀 or rocket icon
Title: Quick Start
Subtitle: Apply the method in 30 minutes
Time: ~30 min
Audience: Curious researchers, first-timers
Prerequisites: git, terminal basics, bun
Steps: 7
CTA: "Start Quick Start"
\`\`\`

**Agent-Assisted (Accent color)**:
\`\`\`
Icon: 🤖 or robot icon
Title: Agent-Assisted Research
Subtitle: Let your AI agent learn the methodology
Time: ~45 min
Audience: Power users with Claude Code or Codex
Prerequisites: Claude Max or GPT Pro subscription
Steps: 8
CTA: "Start Agent-Assisted"
\`\`\`

**Multi-Agent Cockpit (Success color)**:
\`\`\`
Icon: 🎛️ or control panel icon
Title: Multi-Agent Cockpit
Subtitle: Orchestrate a research group
Time: ~2 hours
Audience: Advanced practitioners
Prerequisites: All three CLI agents, ntm, Agent Mail
Steps: 10
CTA: "Start Multi-Agent"
\`\`\`

---

# FAQ Content

**Q: Which path is right for me?**
A: Start with Quick Start if you're new. It requires no special setup and gives you a taste of the methodology. Move to Agent-Assisted if you already use Claude Code or Codex — it's the highest-leverage path. Only choose Multi-Agent if you're ready to run persistent infrastructure.

**Q: What if I get stuck?**
A: Every step has a "Troubleshooting" section. If that doesn't help, check our GitHub Issues or the Discord (if we have one).

**Q: Can I switch paths?**
A: Yes! The paths share some concepts. If Quick Start feels too basic, jump to Agent-Assisted. If Agent-Assisted is missing orchestration, move to Multi-Agent.

**Q: Do I need to pay for AI subscriptions?**
A: Quick Start works with any AI chat interface (even free tiers). Agent-Assisted requires Claude Max or GPT Pro. Multi-Agent requires all three subscriptions.

---

# Testing Requirements

- E2E test: path selection → first step of each path
- Mobile viewport: cards stack vertically
- Keyboard navigation: tab through cards, enter to select
- localStorage: progress persists across sessions

---

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Landing page renders with three path cards
- [ ] Each path links to its first step
- [ ] Layout includes progress sidebar
- [ ] FAQ section is collapsible
- [ ] Mobile-responsive design verified
- [ ] Progress state persists to localStorage
- [ ] Back navigation works from any step

title: Task: Create search modal component
description:
Build the main search modal UI component.

## Purpose

The search modal is the primary interface for search. It must feel instant, intuitive, and polished.

## Design Reference

Inspired by: Linear, Raycast, Notion, Spotlight

## Component Structure

### SearchModal
- Overlay with backdrop blur
- Centered dialog box
- Auto-focus on input
- Close on Escape or backdrop click

### SearchInput
- Large, prominent input field
- Clear button when text present
- Scope toggle (All / Transcripts)
- Optional loading spinner during index load

### SearchResults
- Virtualized list for performance
- Each result shows:
  - Document type badge (color-coded)
  - Document title
  - Section title (if applicable)
  - Context snippet with highlighted matches
- Keyboard navigation (arrow keys)
- Click/Enter to navigate

### Empty States
- No query: Show recent searches or tips
- No results: Helpful message, suggestions
- Loading: Skeleton or spinner

## Interaction

1. Open: ⌘K / Ctrl+K, or click search icon
2. Type: Results appear instantly (debounced)
3. Navigate: Arrow keys move selection
4. Select: Enter or click navigates to result
5. Close: Escape, backdrop click, or successful navigation

## Mobile Adaptations

- Full-width on narrow screens
- Bottom sheet presentation option
- Larger touch targets
- Native keyboard handling

## Files to Create

- `apps/web/src/components/search/SearchModal.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/search/SearchInput.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/search/SearchResults.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/search/SearchResult.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/search/index.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Modal opens on ⌘K and click
- [ ] Input auto-focuses
- [ ] Results appear as user types
- [ ] Keyboard navigation works
- [ ] Mobile-friendly layout
- [ ] Accessible (ARIA, focus management)
- [ ] Smooth animations (60fps)
close_reason: SpotlightSearch.tsx implements complete search modal with all required features (modal, backdrop, keyboard nav, results, highlighting, mobile support)

title: EPIC: Corpus Browser & Document Viewer
description:
# Purpose

The corpus is the foundation of everything - 236 transcript segments plus metaprompts, quote bank, and other documents. Users need to:

1. **Discover** - Browse all documents, filter by type, search by content
2. **Navigate** - Jump to specific sections via TOC, use stable §n anchors
3. **Read** - Beautiful typography, syntax highlighting, comfortable reading experience
4. **Cite** - Copy section references, build excerpt blocks for sessions

# Pages

1. **/corpus** - Document listing with cards, search bar, filters
2. **/corpus/[doc]** - Full document view with TOC sidebar, anchors, citation copy

# Components Needed

- **DocumentCard** - Thumbnail card with title, description, metadata
- **SearchBar** - Full-text search with preview results
- **MarkdownViewer** - Rich renderer with TOC generation, anchor links
- **CopyButton** - For copying citations/excerpts
- **TableOfContents** - Sticky sidebar TOC with scroll highlighting

# Technical Decisions

- Server components for document loading (better SEO, faster initial load)
- Client-side search with prebuilt index (fast, works offline)
- Use rehype/remark plugins for markdown processing
- Generate TOC from heading structure
- §n anchors should be clickable and copyable

# Depends On

- Design System Foundation
close_reason: Superseded by brenner_bot-5so.4.1 (Corpus reader) + brenner_bot-5so.4.2 (Search/excerpt)

title: Bug: harden release workflow dispatch + edge proxy env access
description:
Follow-up hardening discovered during QA.

1) Release workflow safety:
- .github/workflows/release.yml currently gates publish vs dry-run using whether github.ref starts with refs/tags/.
- A workflow_dispatch run against a tag ref could therefore publish release assets.
- Desired behavior: publish only on tag push events; treat all workflow_dispatch runs as dry-runs (build + upload dist artifact only).

2) Edge proxy robustness:
- apps/web/src/proxy.ts should avoid dynamic env access (process.env["BRENNER_TRUST_CF_ACCESS_HEADERS"]).
- In Edge/middleware bundling, dynamic env access can be unreliable; use process.env.BRENNER_TRUST_CF_ACCESS_HEADERS instead.

3) Minor docs/test clarity:
- apps/web/src/lib/artifact-merge.test.ts comment should align with repo rule: run web tests via "cd apps/web && bun run test" (not bun test).

Acceptance:
- workflow_dispatch never publishes release assets (even if run on a tag ref).
- Tag pushes (push on refs/tags/v*) still publish release assets.
- Proxy env gating remains correct and tests pass.
close_reason: Release workflow: publish only on tag push; workflow_dispatch stays dry-run. Edge proxy uses direct env access; updated test comment.

title: Task: Implement Test Storage Layer
description:
# Task: Implement Test Storage Layer

## Objective
Create file-based storage for test records with cross-session indexing.

## Implementation Details

### File Location
`apps/web/src/lib/test-storage.ts`

### Storage Structure
```
.research/
├── tests/
│   ├── RS-20251230-tests.json
│   └── ...
└── test-index.json
```

### Per-Session File Format
```json
{
  "sessionId": "RS-20251230",
  "tests": [
    {
      "id": "T-RS20251230-001",
      "description": "Lineage tracing with Cre-lox to track cell fate",
      "targetHypotheses": [
        {
          "hypothesisId": "H-RS20251230-001",
          "prediction": "If epigenetically determined, daughter cells maintain parental methylation patterns"
        },
        {
          "hypothesisId": "H-RS20251230-002",
          "prediction": "If transcriptionally determined, daughter cells show variable expression patterns"
        }
      ],
      "designedInSession": "RS-20251230",
      "status": "completed",
      "execution": {
        "executedAt": "2025-12-31T10:00:00Z",
        "result": "Daughter cells showed variable methylation but stable expression",
        "matchedPredictions": [],
        "violatedPredictions": ["H-RS20251230-001", "H-RS20251230-002"],
        "confidence": "medium"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Core Functions
```typescript
// CRUD operations
export async function loadSessionTests(sessionId: string): Promise<TestRecord[]>
export async function saveSessionTests(sessionId: string, tests: TestRecord[]): Promise<void>
export async function getTestById(id: string): Promise<TestRecord | null>

// Index operations
export async function rebuildTestIndex(): Promise<void>
export async function getTestsForHypothesis(hypothesisId: string): Promise<TestRecord[]>

// Query operations
export async function getTestsByStatus(status: TestStatus): Promise<TestRecord[]>
export async function getBlockedTests(): Promise<TestRecord[]>
export async function getDesignedButNotExecutedTests(): Promise<TestRecord[]>
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test records stored in per-session JSON files
- [ ] Index enables lookup by hypothesis ID
- [ ] Query by status (designed, completed, blocked)
- [ ] Execution records embedded in test records
- [ ] Git-friendly format (one test per logical unit)

## Dependencies
- Task: Define Test Record and Execution Schemas

## Effort Estimate
~180 lines of code, ~2 hours
close_reason: Test Storage Layer fully implemented in test-storage.ts with 35 passing tests. Includes CRUD operations, cross-session indexing, query operations by status/hypothesis/quality, statistics, and hypothesis coverage tracking.

title: Tutorial Layout: Responsive sidebar + mobile progress header

# Tutorial Layout

The shared layout for all tutorial pages. Provides consistent navigation, progress tracking, and responsive behavior.

## File

\`app/tutorial/layout.tsx\`

## Structure

**Desktop (>= 1024px)**:
\`\`\`
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [Header: BrennerBot logo, nav, theme toggle]             │
├────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [Progress      │ [Main Content]                          │
│  Sidebar]      │                                         │
│                │                                         │
│ Step 1 ✓       │                                         │
│ Step 2 ●       │                                         │
│ Step 3 ○       │                                         │
│ ...            │                                         │
│                │                                         │
│ [Back to       │                                         │
│  Tutorial]     │                                         │
└────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

**Tablet (768px - 1023px)**:
- Sidebar collapses to icons only
- Expands on hover/focus

**Mobile (< 768px)**:
- No sidebar
- Progress in header: "Step 2 of 7 · Quick Start"
- Hamburger menu for path navigation

  currentPath: 'quick-start' | 'agent-assisted' | 'multi-agent' | null;

  goToStep: (step: number) => void;
  goToNextStep: () => void;
  goToPrevStep: () => void;
}
\`\`\`

## State Persistence

- Store in localStorage: \`brenner-tutorial-{pathId}-progress\`
- Load on mount, hydrate UI
- Clear on path completion or manual reset

## Tests

- Desktop layout renders correctly
- Mobile layout collapses properly
- Context provides correct values
- localStorage persistence works
- Navigation between steps works

title: Task: Audit and fix mobile touch targets
description:
Ensure all interactive elements meet touch target requirements.

## Purpose

Touch targets that are too small or too close together cause frustration and errors. This is a common web → mobile failure point.

## Requirements

- Minimum touch target: 44x44px (Apple HIG), 48dp (Material Design)
- Minimum spacing between targets: 8px
- Target should be larger than visual element if needed (padding)

## Elements to Audit

### Navigation
- Header links/buttons
- Bottom nav items (already 44px, verify)
- Breadcrumb links

### Content
- Document links in index pages
- Card components
- Navigation cards (prev/next)

### Interactive
- Toggle switches
- Filter buttons
- Close buttons on modals/sheets
- Theme toggle

### Forms (if any)
- Input fields
- Buttons
- Checkboxes/radios

## Common Fixes

- Increase padding (not just size)
- Use min-height/min-width
- Add touch-action CSS if needed
- Increase spacing between targets

## Testing

- Use Chrome DevTools touch target overlay
- Actually tap on real device
- Test with accessibility settings (large touch accommodation)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All targets >= 44px on their tap dimension
- [ ] Minimum 8px spacing between adjacent targets
- [ ] No accidental taps on wrong element
- [ ] Works with accessibility settings enabled
close_reason: Touch target audit complete: Fixed TOC items to 44px min-height, Tabs component to 44px, close buttons from 32px to 44px (size-11), and button sm/icon-sm variants from 32px to 40px. Added touch-manipulation CSS to interactive elements. Build and all 641 tests pass.

title: Task: Verify 60fps animations on mobile
description:
Ensure all animations run at 60fps on mobile devices.

## Purpose

Janky animations destroy the feeling of quality. 60fps animations feel 'native'.

## Current Animations to Verify

- Page transitions (fade-in-up)
- Card hover states (desktop) / tap states (mobile)
- Bottom sheet open/close
- Search modal open/close
- Reading progress bar
- Back-to-top button appearance

## Testing Method

1. Open Chrome DevTools
2. Performance panel → Frame rate
3. Trigger each animation
4. Verify frames maintain 60fps
5. On actual mobile device if possible

## Common Performance Issues

### Layout Thrashing
- Animating width/height causes reflow
- Use transform instead

### Paint Storms
- Animating colors on large areas
- Use opacity and transform instead

### Compositor Misses
- Not using will-change or translateZ
- Add hints for animated elements

## Optimizations If Needed

```css
.animated-element {
  will-change: transform, opacity;
  transform: translateZ(0); /* Force GPU layer */
}
```

### React Performance
- Memoize animated components
- Avoid re-renders during animation
- Use CSS transitions not JS

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All animations tested in DevTools
- [ ] 60fps maintained for each animation
- [ ] Tested on actual mobile device
- [ ] No jank during scroll
- [ ] No jank during page transitions
- [ ] Bottom sheet smooth
- [ ] Search modal smooth
close_reason: Animation audit complete: All actively used animations (page transitions, bottom sheet, search modal, toasts, etc.) use only GPU-accelerated properties (opacity, transform). The only layout-triggering animation (typewriter using width) is defined but not used in the codebase. No issues found that would cause sub-60fps performance.

Add a CLI diagnostic that makes delta-format problems obvious *before* operators waste time compiling.

`./brenner.ts session diagnose --thread-id <id> [--project-key <abs-path>]`

- No network calls beyond Agent Mail.
- Unit tests cover a thread with (a) valid fenced deltas, (b) inline JSON, (c) no deltas.

title: Feature: Critique Registry
description:
# Feature: Critique Registry

## Purpose
Track adversarial critiques as first-class entities with targets, responses, and resolution status. This enables the "Adversarial Critic" role to have persistent, trackable output.

## Why This Is Needed

The Brenner method has an explicit **Adversarial Critic** role:
- Artifact Schema Section 7: Adversarial Critique
- Evaluation rubric dimensions: "Theory Kill Justification" (0-3), "Real Third Alternative" (0-3)
- Scorecard's "Adversarial Pressure" dimension requires critique data!

Current gap: Critiques exist only as text. We can't:
- Track which critiques have been addressed
- Answer "what's the strongest attack on H1?"
- Measure adversarial pressure objectively

From §229: "When they go ugly, kill them" — but kills should be JUSTIFIED by critiques!

## Schema Design

```typescript
export const CritiqueTargetTypeSchema = z.enum([
  'hypothesis',    // Attacks a specific hypothesis
  'test',          // Attacks a test design
  'assumption',    // Attacks an assumption
  'framing',       // Attacks the research thread itself
  'methodology',   // Attacks the overall approach
]);

export const CritiqueStatusSchema = z.enum([
  'active',      // Critique not yet addressed
  'addressed',   // Response provided
  'dismissed',   // Rejected as invalid
  'accepted',    // Critique accepted, changes made
]);

export const CritiqueSchema = z.object({
  /** Stable ID: C-{session_id}-{sequence} */
  id: z.string().regex(/^C-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}$/),
  
  /** What type of thing is being attacked? */
  targetType: CritiqueTargetTypeSchema,
  
  /** The ID of what's being attacked (H-xxx, T-xxx, A-xxx, or null for framing) */
  targetId: z.string().optional(),
  
  /** The attack: how could this be fundamentally wrong? */
  attack: z.string().min(20),
  
  /** What evidence would confirm this critique? */
  evidenceToConfirm: z.string().min(10),
  
  /** Does this propose a constructive alternative? */
  proposedAlternative: z.object({
    description: z.string(),
    mechanism: z.string().optional(),
    testable: z.boolean(),
  }).optional(),
  
  /** Current status */
  status: CritiqueStatusSchema,
  
  /** Response to the critique (if addressed) */
  response: z.object({
    text: z.string(),
    respondedBy: z.string().optional(),
    respondedAt: z.string().datetime(),
    actionTaken: z.enum(['none', 'modified', 'killed', 'new_test']).optional(),
  }).optional(),
  
  /** Severity: how serious is this threat? */
  severity: z.enum(['minor', 'moderate', 'serious', 'critical']),
  
  /** Session where this was recorded */
  sessionId: z.string(),
  
  /** Who raised this critique? */
  raisedBy: z.string().optional(),  // Agent name
  
  /** §n transcript anchors if grounded in Brenner */
  anchors: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  
  /** Timestamps */
  createdAt: z.string().datetime(),
  updatedAt: z.string().datetime(),
});
```

## Critique Quality Scoring

From evaluation rubric:

**Theory Kill Justification (0-3)** — when a KILL is proposed:
- 0: Kill based on aesthetic preference or convenience
- 1: Kill based on single piece of weak evidence
- 2: Kill with multiple evidence points but room for doubt
- 3: Kill is decisive: direct contradiction, no rescue moves

**Real Third Alternative (0-3)** — critique proposes constructive alternative:
- 0: Pure skepticism ("we don't know")
- 1: Alternative is vague
- 2: Specific alternative but not fully developed
- 3: Concrete alternative with mechanism and testable predictions

## Critique Workflow

```
1. Adversarial Critic raises critique C1 targeting H1
     ↓
2. Critique recorded with attack, evidenceToConfirm, severity
     ↓
3. Hypothesis Generator or Test Designer responds
     ↓
4. Response recorded, status updated
     ↓
5. If accepted: hypothesis modified, killed, or new test designed
```

## Unaddressed Critiques

Unaddressed critiques WEAKEN the target:
- A hypothesis with 3 unaddressed critiques is "under attack"
- Dashboard shows "hypotheses with unaddressed critiques"
- Scorecard penalizes unaddressed serious critiques

## CLI Commands

- `brenner critique list [--status=active|addressed|dismissed|accepted] [--target=<id>]`
- `brenner critique show <id>`
- `brenner critique create --target=H1 --attack="..." --evidence-to-confirm="..."`
- `brenner critique respond <id> --response="..." [--action=modified|killed|new_test]`
- `brenner critique dismiss <id> --reason="..."`
- `brenner critique accept <id>`

## Integration Points

- **Hypothesis Registry**: Hypotheses gain `linkedCritiques`, `unresolvedCritiqueCount`
- **Test Binding**: Tests gain `linkedCritiques`
- **Assumption Registry**: Assumptions gain `linkedCritiques`
- **Scorecard**: "Adversarial Pressure" dimension now has data source
- **Dashboard**: Show "hypotheses under attack" (high unaddressed critique count)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Critique schema defined with all target types
- [ ] Response tracking with action taken
- [ ] Severity levels for prioritization
- [ ] Unaddressed critique flagging
- [ ] CLI commands for full CRUD + response workflow
- [ ] Integration with hypotheses, tests, assumptions

## Tasks (to be created)

1. Define Critique Zod Schema
2. Implement Critique Storage Layer
3. Implement Critique Response Workflow
4. Create Critique CLI Commands
5. Write Critique Module Unit Tests
6. Integrate with Hypothesis/Test/Assumption Registries
close_reason: Critique Registry delivered: schema+workflow (critique.ts), storage+index (CritiqueStorage), CLI surface (brenner.ts critique subcommands), and unit coverage (critique.test.ts + critique-storage.test.ts).

title: EPIC: Product Landing Page - World-Class Brenner Lab Showcase
description:
# World-Class Product Landing Page for Brenner Lab Mode

## Overview
Create a stunning, Stripe-quality landing page that showcases the full Brenner Lab Mode system - the CLI, multi-agent orchestration, session management, and all research workflow features. This page should make visitors gasp at its polish and immediately understand why this system is transformative for AI-assisted research.

## Strategic Context
While Brenner Bot is 100% free and open source, we want the landing page to have the production quality and persuasive clarity of a premium SaaS product. This serves multiple purposes:
1. **Credibility**: Shows the project is serious and well-maintained
2. **Comprehension**: Complex systems need excellent UX to be understood
3. **Adoption**: Lower barrier to entry through clear, compelling presentation
4. **Community**: Attracts contributors who appreciate quality

## Key Differentiator
This page focuses on the **operational** aspects of Brenner Bot - actually RUNNING research sessions, orchestrating agents, and producing artifacts. It's NOT about the learning corpus or transcripts (which have their own pages), but about the research workflow system itself.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL: Page Order vs Implementation Order

These are DIFFERENT concepts:
- **Implementation order** = What must be built first (driven by dependencies)
- **Page order** = What appears first when scrolling (driven by user psychology)

### Recommended PAGE ORDER (scroll order on the page)

| Position | Section | Why Here |
|----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Hero (f8vs.1) | First impression, value prop |
| 2 | Multi-Agent Orchestration (f8vs.3) | **The "wow" factor** - lead with excitement! |
| 3 | Core Research Workflow (f8vs.2) | Now they want to know HOW it works |
| 4 | Discovery & Intelligence (f8vs.5) | Smart features keep interest |
| 5 | Quality Assurance (f8vs.4) | Trust-building, now they're invested |
| 6 | Technical Architecture (f8vs.7) | For developers checking it out |
| 7 | Operator Framework (f8vs.6) | Deep dive for intellectually curious ⚠️ |
| 8 | Get Started (f8vs.8) | Convert interest to action |

**Key insight**: Multi-Agent (f8vs.3) is the most exciting/differentiated feature - it should be SECOND, not third! Lead with the "wow" factor.

**Warning on f8vs.6**: The Operator Framework uses mathematical notation (⊘, ✂, ⟂, ⊞) that may alienate non-academic visitors. Position it near the end and consider making it an expandable/optional section.

## CRITICAL: The Selling Approach

### Problem-Solution Framing
Every section must answer: "What problem does this solve? Why should I care?"

| Problem (Current State) | Solution (Brenner Lab) |
|------------------------|------------------------|
| AI chats are ephemeral and messy | Persistent, auditable, reproducible sessions |
| Hindsight bias corrupts research | Prediction Lock forces commitment before results |
| Single AI perspective has blind spots | Multi-agent debate surfaces what one model misses |
| Research often lacks rigor | 50+ linting rules enforce research hygiene |
| You keep re-investigating the same questions | Similarity search finds your related past work |
| Overconfidence in predictions | Calibration tracking reveals your actual accuracy |
| Hard to know which hypotheses are solid | Robustness scoring shows battle-tested ideas |
| Evidence gets lost in chat history | Citation system with proper anchoring |

### CLI-Forward Presentation
Every feature section should include at least one `brenner` CLI command showing how to actually USE the feature:

```bash
# Session management
brenner session start --thread-id RS-20260105 --question "..."
brenner session status --thread-id RS-20260105 --watch
brenner session compile --thread-id RS-20260105

# Corpus access
brenner corpus search "discriminative test"
brenner excerpt build --sections 58,78

# Diagnostics
brenner doctor --skip-ntm --skip-cass
```

### Compelling Language Guidelines
- Use active voice: "Lock your predictions" not "Predictions are locked"
- Focus on outcomes: "Never lose a hypothesis" not "Stores hypotheses"
- Be specific: "50+ linting rules" not "Many quality checks"
- Show, don't tell: Animated demos > static descriptions

## What Must Be Showcased

### Core Research Workflow
- Session State Machine (11 phases from intake to completion)
- Hypothesis lifecycle management (proposed → active → killed/validated)
- Evidence gathering and citation system
- Test design and execution tracking

### Multi-Agent Orchestration
- Agent Debate Mode (Oxford, Socratic, Steelman formats)
- Tribunal agents with specialized roles
- Agent Mail coordination bus
- Deterministic artifact merging

### Quality Assurance Systems
- Coach Mode for guided learning
- Prediction Lock to prevent hindsight bias
- Calibration tracking for researcher accuracy
- 50+ linting rules for research hygiene
- Confound detection across 8 research domains

### Discovery & Intelligence
- Hypothesis Similarity Search (hash-based embeddings)
- What-If Scenario exploration
- Robustness scoring
- Anomaly detection and quarantine

### Technical Excellence
- CLI-first architecture (no API keys needed)
- Offline-first with sync
- Undo/Redo for all operations
- Session replay and debugging

## UI/UX North Star
Stripe's marketing pages are the gold standard:
- Obsessive attention to micro-interactions
- Generous whitespace and clear visual hierarchy
- Animations that enhance understanding, not distract
- Mobile experience that's equally stunning
- Dark/light mode support
- Performance that feels instant

## Navigation Strategy
No new navbar item - link from the primary landing page with a clear CTA like "Explore Lab Mode →" or "See the Research System →"

## Implementation Order (Dependency-Driven)

**Note**: This is BUILD order, not PAGE order. See "Page Order" section above.

```
Foundation Layer (parallel, start first):
├── f8vs.9: Animation & Scroll Effects System
└── f8vs.10: Mobile-First Responsive Design

Visual Identity (after foundation):
└── f8vs.1: Hero Section & Visual Identity System
    └── depends on f8vs.9 + f8vs.10

Content Sections (parallel, after hero):
├── f8vs.2: Core Research Workflow Section
├── f8vs.3: Multi-Agent Orchestration Section
├── f8vs.4: Quality Assurance & Research Hygiene Section
├── f8vs.5: Discovery & Intelligence Section
├── f8vs.6: Operator Framework Section
└── f8vs.7: Technical Architecture Section
    └── all depend on f8vs.1

Final CTA (after all content):
└── f8vs.8: Get Started & CTA Section
    └── depends on f8vs.2-7
```

## Success Criteria
1. Visitors immediately understand the value proposition
2. Mobile experience is as polished as desktop
3. Page load is < 2s with smooth animations
4. Accessibility score > 95 on Lighthouse
5. Zero layout shift during scroll animations
6. Every feature section includes a CLI command example
7. Problem/solution framing is clear in every section

title: Feature: Mobile-First Responsive Design
description:
# Mobile-First Responsive Design

## Purpose
Ensure the landing page is not just "responsive" but genuinely excellent on mobile. Mobile users should have an experience designed for touch, not a shrunk desktop site.

## Design Philosophy

### Mobile Is Not Desktop Lite
- Different content hierarchy for small screens
- Touch-optimized interactions
- Vertical rhythm and scroll experience
- Battery and bandwidth conscious

### Touch-First Interactions
- 44px minimum touch targets
- Swipe gestures where natural
- No hover-dependent features
- Immediate feedback on touch

### Performance Priority
- Critical CSS inlined
- Images lazy-loaded with proper srcset
- Minimal JavaScript for initial render
- Target: < 2s meaningful paint on 3G

## Breakpoint Strategy

### Breakpoints
- Mobile: 0-639px (default)
- Tablet: 640-1023px (sm:)
- Desktop: 1024-1279px (lg:)
- Wide: 1280px+ (xl:)

### Mobile (< 640px)

#### Hero Section
- Full-width, no side padding hero
- Stacked: headline → visualization → CTAs
- Smaller headline (32px vs 48px)
- Single-column CTA buttons
- Visualization simplified or auto-playing

#### Content Sections
- Single column throughout
- Cards stack vertically
- Horizontal scroll for galleries
- Collapsible for long content

#### Navigation
- Hamburger menu for secondary nav
- Bottom sticky bar for primary CTA
- Breadcrumbs as horizontal scroll

#### Typography
- Body: 16px (never smaller for readability)
- Headlines: 24-32px
- Line height: 1.6 for body text
- Generous paragraph spacing

### Tablet (640-1023px)

#### Hero Section
- Two-column possible (50/50)
- Medium headline size (40px)
- Visualization can be larger

#### Content Sections
- 2-column grids for cards
- Side-by-side comparisons possible
- Tables become horizontally scrollable

### Desktop (1024px+)

#### Full Experience
- All animations enabled
- Hover effects active
- Multi-column layouts
- Large visualizations

## Mobile-Specific Components

### Swipeable Card Carousel
For feature cards, agent profiles, etc.
- Dots indicator below
- Snap scrolling
- Peek next card (shows it continues)
- Touch velocity for momentum

### Expandable Sections
For detailed content:
- Collapsed by default
- Clear expand/collapse affordance
- Smooth height animation
- Remember expanded state

### Bottom Sheet
For detailed views:
- Swipe up to expand
- Swipe down to close
- Handles at top
- Backdrop blur

### Sticky CTA Bar
- Fixed at bottom of viewport
- Primary action always visible
- Appears after scrolling past hero
- Subtle shadow for depth

## Touch Interactions

### Tap
- Immediate visual feedback (scale/opacity)
- 44px minimum target
- Generous spacing between targets

### Swipe
- Natural for carousels
- Gesture hints for new users
- Edge swipe avoided (browser conflict)

### Pull-to-Refresh
- Not needed for static landing page
- But smooth scroll at top

### Long Press
- Not used (confusing pattern)

## Performance Optimizations

### Images
- WebP with PNG fallback
- srcset for density variations
- Lazy loading below fold
- Placeholder blur or skeleton

### Fonts
- System font stack preferred
- If custom: subset, preload, font-display: swap
- Maximum 2 font weights loaded

### JavaScript
- Code split by route
- Dynamic import for below-fold sections
- No blocking scripts
- Service worker for repeat visits

### CSS
- Critical CSS inlined (< 14KB)
- Unused styles tree-shaken
- No render-blocking stylesheets

## Testing Requirements

### Devices to Test
- iPhone SE (small)
- iPhone 14 Pro (medium)
- iPhone 14 Pro Max (large)
- iPad Mini (tablet)
- Various Android sizes

### Conditions to Test
- Portrait and landscape
- With/without notch (safe areas)
- Different font sizes (accessibility)
- Slow 3G connection
- Offline (should show something)

### Metrics Targets
- Lighthouse Mobile: > 90
- First Contentful Paint: < 1.5s
- Largest Contentful Paint: < 2.5s
- Cumulative Layout Shift: < 0.1
- First Input Delay: < 100ms

## Common Mobile Pitfalls to Avoid
- Horizontal scroll on full page
- Tiny touch targets
- Hover-only interactions
- Fixed headers that eat viewport
- Form inputs that trigger zoom
- Slow-loading hero images
- Carousels that hijack scroll

# Operator Framework Section

## ⚠️ RISK ASSESSMENT

**This section may alienate non-academic visitors.**

The mathematical notation (⊘, ✂, ⟂, ⊞) and abstract composition formula are intellectually exciting for the right audience, but may:
- Overwhelm casual visitors
- Create a "this isn't for me" feeling
- Break the flow of the page narrative

**Mitigations:**
1. **Position**: Place near the end of the page (position 7 of 8), after trust has been established
2. **Framing**: Label as "Deep Dive" or "For the Curious" to set expectations
3. **Progressive disclosure**: Default to collapsed/minimal, expand on click
4. **Alternative entry**: Offer a simpler "plain English" version alongside the notation
5. **Exit ramp**: Ensure users can skip directly to "Get Started" if overwhelmed

**Decision needed during implementation**: Consider whether this section should be:
- A full section on the landing page (current plan)
- An expandable subsection within another feature
- A linked separate page for deep dives

## Purpose
Show the cognitive operators that encode Brenner's methodology. This is intellectually exciting - showing how abstract thinking patterns become composable, executable functions.

## Key Messages
1. Brenner's methods encoded as operators
2. Operators are composable into pipelines
3. Each operator has templates to get started
4. Mathematical notation makes the method precise

## Content Structure

### Section Title
"The Operator Algebra: Brenner's Methods as Executable Code"

### Introduction
"Sydney Brenner's breakthrough wasn't just his discoveries - it was his method. We've encoded his cognitive patterns as composable operators that you can apply systematically."

### Plain English Version (NEW - offer first)
Before the mathematical notation, offer a simpler framing:

> **The Brenner Method in 4 Steps:**
> 1. **Split the levels** - Separate the "what" from the "how"
> 2. **Design killing tests** - Find experiments that eliminate possibilities
> 3. **Choose your system** - Pick the easiest organism/model to test with
> 4. **Check the physics** - Make sure it's physically possible

*"Want the precise notation? Expand below."*

### Core Operators Display

#### ⊘ Level-Split
**"Separate program from interpreter"**
- Message vs machine, genotype vs phenotype
- Includes "chastity vs impotence" diagnostic
- Template: "What is the information? What is the mechanism?"

Visual: Split diagram showing two levels with examples

#### ✂ Exclusion-Test  
**"Design tests that eliminate, not confirm"**
- Forbidden patterns: what cannot occur if H is true
- Discriminative power rating (1-5)
- Template: "If H1 is true, we should NEVER see..."

Visual: Hypothesis tree with branches being pruned

#### ⟂ Object-Transpose
**"Change the system until the test is easy"**
- Choose organism/model strategically
- "The experimental object is a design variable"
- Template: "What system would make this test cheap and unambiguous?"

Visual: Multiple organisms/systems with selection arrow

#### ⊞ Scale-Check
**"Stay imprisoned in physics"**
- Validate against physical constraints
- Calculate timescales, length scales, energy scales
- Template: "Is this physically possible at the relevant scale?"

Visual: Scale bars with constraint ranges

### The Core Composition (Expandable by default on desktop, collapsed on mobile)
"The signature Brenner move expressed as operator composition:"

```
(⌂ ∘ ✂ ∘ ≡ ∘ ⊘) powered by (↑ ∘ ⟂ ∘ 🔧) constrained by (⊞) kept honest by (ΔE ∘ †)
```

Expanded explanation:
- Start from a paradox (◊)
- Split levels (⊘)
- Extract invariants (≡)
- Design exclusion tests (✂)
- Materialize as decision procedure (⌂)
- Power by amplification (↑) in well-chosen system (⟂) you build yourself (🔧)
- Constrain by physics (⊞)
- Keep honest with exception handling (ΔE) and theory killing (†)

### Extended Operators (collapsed by default)

- ◊ Paradox-hunt: Use contradictions as beacons
- ⊕ Cross-domain: Import tools from other fields

- † Theory-kill: Drop hypotheses when the world says no
- ⌂ Materialize: "What would I see if this were true?"

### Code Example
```typescript

const brennerPipeline = pipe(
  levelSplit,        // Separate levels
  invariantExtract,  // Find what survives
  exclusionTest,     // Design killing experiments
  materialize,       // Compile to decision procedure
);

const result = brennerPipeline(hypothesis, context);
```

# Technical Architecture Section

## Purpose
Build trust with technical users by showing the solid engineering foundation. Highlight the CLI-first design, offline capabilities, and security model.

## Key Messages
1. CLI-first: No API keys in code, use your own subscriptions
2. Local-first: Works offline, syncs when connected
3. Deterministic: Same inputs always produce same outputs
4. Auditable: Every action tracked and reversible

## Content Structure

### Section Title
"Built for Serious Work: Architecture That Respects Your Research"

### Key Architecture Points

#### CLI-First Design
**"Your Terminal, Your Subscriptions, Your Control"**

"Brenner Lab doesn't call AI APIs from code. Instead, CLI tools run in your terminal under your existing subscriptions (Claude Max, GPT Pro, Gemini Ultra). You see everything, control everything."

Benefits:
- No API keys to manage or leak
- No rate limits beyond your subscription
- Full session context preserved
- Real-time visibility into agent work

Visual: Terminal with agents running in tmux panes

#### Local-First Storage
**"Your Data Stays With You"**

"Hypotheses, evidence, and session artifacts are stored locally. The system works offline and syncs when you're ready."

Components:
- IndexedDB for structured data
- localStorage for queue state
- File locks for concurrent access
- Background sync when online

Visual: Data flow diagram showing local storage → optional cloud sync

#### Deterministic Merging
**"Reproducible by Design"**

"When multiple agents produce outputs, they merge deterministically. Two runs with the same inputs produce identical outputs."

Merge rules:
- Timestamp ordering
- Last-write-wins for conflicts
- Killed items preserved in history
- Conflicts logged for audit

Visual: Merge diagram showing deltas combining

#### Security Model
**"Fail-Closed, Not Fail-Open"**

"Lab Mode is protected by default. Unauthorized requests get 404 (no information leakage), not 401."

Layers:
1. Environment check (BRENNER_LAB_MODE)
2. Authentication (Cloudflare Access or lab secret)
3. Timing-safe secret comparison
4. Content policy enforcement

### The Join-Key Contract
"Thread ID is the universal join key that ties everything together:"

```
Thread ID ↔ Agent Mail thread
         ↔ ntm session
         ↔ Artifact file path
         ↔ Beads issue ID
```

Visual: Diagram showing thread ID connecting all components

### CLI Command Showcase
Selected commands with brief descriptions:

```bash
# Search the corpus
brenner corpus search "exclusion test"

# Start a session
brenner session start --thread-id RS-20251230-cell-fate \

# Check session status
brenner session status --thread-id RS-20251230-cell-fate --watch

# Compile artifacts
brenner session compile --thread-id RS-20251230-cell-fate
```

### Performance Stats
- CLI startup: < 50ms
- Artifact compilation: < 50ms
- Test suite: 4300+ tests, < 30s
- Page load: < 2s target

title: Feature: Animation & Scroll Effects System
description:
# Animation & Scroll Effects System

## Purpose
Create a cohesive animation system that enhances understanding without overwhelming. Animations should feel purposeful, performant, and delightful.

## Key Principles

### 1. Purpose Over Polish
Every animation should serve a purpose:
- Guide attention to important elements
- Show relationships between concepts
- Provide feedback for interactions
- Create smooth transitions between states

### 2. Performance First
- Use CSS transforms and opacity (GPU-accelerated)
- Avoid animating layout properties (width, height, margin)
- Use will-change sparingly and remove after animation
- Target 60fps on mid-range devices

### 3. Accessibility
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion
- Provide static fallbacks
- Don't hide content behind animations
- Ensure animations don't trigger vestibular issues

## Animation Inventory

### Entry Animations (on scroll into view)

#### Fade Up
- Elements fade in while moving up 20-30px
- Duration: 400-600ms
- Easing: ease-out
- Use for: Text blocks, cards, images

#### Stagger Reveal
- Multiple items animate in sequence
- Stagger delay: 50-100ms per item
- Use for: Lists, grids, feature cards

#### Scale In
- Element scales from 0.95 to 1 with fade
- Duration: 300-400ms
- Use for: Buttons, badges, icons

#### Draw In
- SVG paths draw themselves
- Duration: 800-1200ms
- Use for: Diagrams, connection lines, icons

### Scroll-Linked Animations

#### Parallax
- Background elements move slower than foreground
- Factor: 0.3-0.5x scroll speed
- Use for: Hero backgrounds, decorative elements

#### Progress-Linked
- Element state tied to scroll progress
- Example: Timeline fills as user scrolls
- Use for: Timelines, progress indicators

#### Reveal on Threshold
- Elements animate when 20-30% visible
- Use IntersectionObserver for performance
- Use for: All content sections

### Micro-Interactions

#### Button Hover
- Scale to 1.02-1.05
- Subtle shadow increase
- Background color shift
- Duration: 150-200ms

#### Card Hover (Desktop)
- Lift effect (translateY: -4px)
- Shadow increase
- Optional 3D tilt (rotateX/Y based on cursor position)
- Duration: 200-300ms

#### Focus States
- Visible focus ring for keyboard navigation
- Smooth transition to focus state
- Consistent across all interactive elements

#### Click/Tap Feedback
- Quick scale down (0.97) then up (1.0)
- Duration: 100-150ms
- Audio feedback consideration (optional)

### Transition Animations

#### Section to Section
- Smooth scroll with easing
- Intersection-based content loading
- No jarring jumps

#### Modal/Panel Open
- Fade + scale from 0.95
- Backdrop blur (if supported)
- Duration: 200-300ms

#### Accordion Expand
- Height animation with overflow handling
- Content fades in after expand
- Duration: 300-400ms

## Implementation Details

### Framer Motion Configuration
```typescript
// Shared animation variants
export const fadeUp = {
  hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 20 },
  visible: { opacity: 1, y: 0 },
};

export const stagger = {
  visible: {
    transition: {
      staggerChildren: 0.1,
    },
  },
};

// Scroll-triggered component
function AnimateOnScroll({ children }) {
  return (
    <motion.div
      initial="hidden"
      whileInView="visible"
      viewport={{ once: true, margin: "-100px" }}
      variants={fadeUp}
      transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: "easeOut" }}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}
```

### Reduced Motion Support
```typescript
// Hook for respecting user preference
function useReducedMotion() {
  return typeof window !== 'undefined' 
    ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches 
    : false;
}

// Usage
const prefersReducedMotion = useReducedMotion();
const animationDuration = prefersReducedMotion ? 0 : 0.5;
```

### Performance Monitoring
- Use Framer Motion's useReducedMotion
- Monitor frame rate in development
- Test on low-end devices
- Profile with Chrome DevTools

## Animation Timing Guidelines

| Animation Type | Duration | Easing |
|----------------|----------|--------|
| Micro-interaction | 100-200ms | ease-out |
| Content reveal | 400-600ms | ease-out |
| Complex diagram | 800-1200ms | ease-in-out |
| Page transition | 300-500ms | ease-in-out |
| Loading state | 1000ms+ | linear (for spinners) |

## Testing Checklist
- [ ] Works at 60fps on Chrome/Firefox/Safari
- [ ] Respects prefers-reduced-motion
- [ ] No layout shift during animations
- [ ] Keyboard focus visible during animations
- [ ] Touch targets remain accessible
- [ ] Animations don't block content access

## Goal
Write glossary entries for BrennerBot-specific terminology and tooling.

1. **agent-mail**: Message bus for multi-agent coordination
2. **agent-identity**: Named agent (adjective+noun) registered with Agent Mail

11. **corpus**: The complete collection of source documents
12. **transcript**: The 236-segment Brenner interview collection
13. **quote-bank**: Curated verbatim quotes indexed by operator/motif
14. **distillation**: Frontier model's synthesis of Brenner's methodology
15. **metaprompt**: Structured prompt template for applying Brenner method

### Tools
16. **beads**: Issue tracking system (bd command)

title: Feature: Search Infrastructure
description:
Build the core search infrastructure: index generation, storage, and query engine.

## Rationale

Before building UI, we need the search engine working. This is the foundation everything else depends on.

## Technical Decision: Client-Side Search

**Why client-side over server-side:**
- Corpus is small (~589KB text, ~68k words)
- Zero latency after initial load
- Works offline
- Simpler infrastructure (no search server)
- Fits in browser memory easily

**Library choice: FlexSearch**
- Fastest full-text search for JavaScript
- Supports partial matching and relevance scoring
- Small bundle size (~6KB gzipped core)
- Used by VS Code, Notion, others

Alternative: MiniSearch (smaller, good enough for our needs)

## Architecture

### Index Generation
- Run at BUILD TIME (not runtime)
- Parse all corpus documents
- Extract: title, content, section anchors, document type
- Output: JSON index file for client consumption

### Index Contents
For each searchable unit (section/paragraph):
```
{
  docId: string,
  docTitle: string,
  sectionId: string,
  sectionTitle: string,
  content: string,
  anchor: string (for linking)
}
```

### Query Engine
- Debounced search (150ms after typing stops)
- Return top N results with relevance scores
- Include context snippets around matches

## Deliverables

- Build-time index generation script
- Search index JSON file
- Client-side query engine wrapper
- Unit tests for search accuracy

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Index generated at build time
- [ ] Index includes all 7 corpus documents
- [ ] Search returns results in <50ms
- [ ] Relevance ranking works (exact matches higher)
- [ ] Index size < 150KB compressed
close_reason: All 4 subtasks closed. Build-time index generation via MiniSearch, 7 documents indexed, fast search (<50ms), relevance ranking implemented in computeScore function. Index size ~150KB.

title: Fix artifact merge: ignore payload id/kill fields
description:
## Problem
The artifact merge algorithm currently allows delta payloads to overwrite system-owned fields like `id` and kill metadata (e.g. `killed`, `killed_by`, `killed_at`, `kill_reason`).

### Why this matters
Per `specs/artifact_delta_spec_v0.1.md`, IDs are assigned by the merge for `ADD` operations ("target_id MUST be null (ID will be assigned by merge)"). Allowing a payload to set or mutate `id` breaks determinism + referential integrity and can create collisions or confusing artifacts.
Similarly, kill fields should only be mutated by the `KILL` operation (audit trail / semantics).

## Root cause
In `apps/web/src/lib/artifact-merge.ts`:
- `applyAdd` builds new items as `{ id: newId, ...payload }`, so payload can override `id`.
- Research thread creation does `{ id: "RT", ..., ...payload }`, so payload can override `id`.
- `applyEdit` loops over payload keys and will write `id` / kill fields directly onto existing items.

## Fix
- In `ADD`: explicitly ignore/strip `id` and kill fields from payload; always set `id` after payload.
- In `EDIT`: ignore attempts to edit `id` or kill metadata.
- Add focused unit tests proving payload cannot override `id` (ADD + EDIT + research_thread creation).

## Done when
- New tests pass and prevent regressions.
- `apps/web` unit tests + build pass.
close_reason: Artifact merge now ignores system-owned id/kill fields for ADD/EDIT + research_thread creation; added unit tests.

# EPIC: Research Intelligence System

## The Gap This Fills

The Brenner method is fundamentally about **killing hypotheses** — treating them as "mistresses to be discarded once the pleasure is over" (§229). The system produces artifacts with hypothesis slates, discriminative tests, assumption ledgers, anomaly registers, and adversarial critiques. But there's no infrastructure for:

1. **Tracking hypothesis lifecycle** — A hypothesis born in Session 1 might be refined in Session 3 and killed in Session 7. Currently, hypotheses exist only as disconnected items in artifact files.

2. **Tracking assumptions** — Scale checks and background assumptions are critical but not first-class entities. When an assumption is falsified, which hypotheses are affected?

3. **Tracking anomalies** — Paradoxes and surprising observations drive the method (§103: "Both could be wrong"), but they exist only as text.

4. **Tracking critiques** — The Adversarial Critic role produces attacks, but there's no way to track which critiques have been addressed.

5. **Closing the research loop** — Tests are designed but not formally connected to their execution or results.

6. **Method feedback** — The evaluation_rubric_v0.1.md defines 14 scoring criteria, but there's no implementation.

## The Six Registries

This epic builds **four first-class registries** that map to artifact schema sections:

### 1. Hypothesis Registry
- Maps to Artifact Schema Section 2: Hypothesis Slate
- Stable IDs (H-xxx), lifecycle states, cross-session linking
- Fields: statement, mechanism, confidence, category, anchors, linkedAssumptions, linkedAnomalies

### 2. Assumption Registry (NEW)
- Maps to Artifact Schema Section 5: Assumption Ledger
- Types: background, methodological, boundary, scale_physics
- States: unchecked → challenged → verified/falsified
- **Key**: Every program MUST have at least one scale_physics assumption (§58: imprisoned imagination)
- Falsification cascades to dependent hypotheses and tests

### 3. Anomaly Registry (NEW)
- Maps to Artifact Schema Section 6: Anomaly Register
- Quarantine status: active → resolved/deferred/paradigm_shifting
- Conflict tracking: which hypotheses/assumptions does this challenge?
- **Key**: Anomalies can SPAWN hypotheses (paradox grounding)

### 4. Critique Registry (NEW)
- Maps to Artifact Schema Section 7: Adversarial Critique
- Target types: hypothesis, test, assumption, framing
- Response workflow: active → addressed/dismissed/accepted
- **Key**: Unaddressed critiques weaken targets; dashboard shows "hypotheses under attack"

### 5. Prediction Registry (via Test Binding)
- Maps to Artifact Schema Section 3: Predictions Table
- First-class predictions separate from tests
- Per-hypothesis expected outcomes

### 6. Test Registry (via Test Binding)
- Maps to Artifact Schema Section 4: Discriminative Tests
- **MANDATORY**: Potency checks (distinguishes "no effect" from "assay failed")
- Evidence-per-week scoring (4 dimensions, 0-12 total)
- Test→Prediction→Hypothesis binding

## Scorecard: 14-Criterion Evaluation

The Brenner Method Scorecard aligns with evaluation_rubric_v0.1.md:

**Universal (all roles):**
1. Structural Correctness (0-3)
2. Citation Compliance (0-3)
3. Rationale Quality (0-3)

**Hypothesis Generator (Codex):**
4. Level Separation (0-3, weight 1.5)
5. Third Alternative Presence (0-3, weight 2.0)
6. Paradox Exploitation (0-2, optional)

**Test Designer (Opus):**
7. Discriminative Power (0-3, weight 2.0)
8. Potency Check Sufficiency (0-3, weight 2.0)
9. Object Transposition Considered (0-2, optional)
10. Score Calibration Honesty (0-2)

**Adversarial Critic (Gemini):**
11. Scale Check Rigor (0-3, weight 1.5)
12. Anomaly Quarantine Discipline (0-3, weight 1.5)
13. Theory Kill Justification (0-3, when KILL, weight 1.5)
14. Real Third Alternative (0-3, weight 1.5)

## Research Program Dashboard

Aggregates all registries into program-level view:
- Hypothesis funnel (by state and origin type)
- Assumption health (scale checks, falsifications)
- Anomaly status (unresolved puzzles)
- Critique pressure (hypotheses under attack)
- Test execution (potency coverage, evidence scores)
- Timeline of all major events

## Feature Dependency Structure

```
Hypothesis Registry (foundation) ──────────────────┐
        ↓                                          │
Hypothesis Lifecycle States ───────────────────────┤
        ↓                                          │
Test→Hypothesis Binding (with Predictions)         │
        ↓                                          │
Assumption Registry ───────────────────────────────┤
        ↓                                          │
Anomaly Registry ──────────────────────────────────┤
        ↓                                          │
Critique Registry ─────────────────────────────────┤
        ↓                                          │
Brenner Method Scorecard ←─────────────────────────┘
        ↓                         (all registries feed)
Research Program Dashboard
```

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Hypotheses have stable IDs with full metadata (mechanism, anchors, etc.)
- [ ] Hypothesis lifecycle states tracked with transition history
- [ ] Test→Prediction→Hypothesis binding with potency checks
- [ ] Assumption registry with scale_physics enforcement
- [ ] Anomaly registry with hypothesis spawning
- [ ] Critique registry with response workflow
- [ ] 14-criterion scorecard computed per session
- [ ] Program dashboard aggregates all registries

## Non-Goals

- Not predictive analytics (what will be killed next)
- Not automated test execution
- Not replacing human judgment on method quality

Research Intelligence System now has: Hypothesis Registry, Assumption Registry, Anomaly Registry, Critique Registry, Test Registry, Scorecard, Research Program Dashboard, Artifact Semantic Diff, Cross-Session Linking, Session Replay, and Operator Intervention Audit Trail.

- Landing Page (for navigation)

title: Bug: install.sh --easy-mode should create fish config dir
description:
# Problem
When `install.sh` runs with `--easy-mode`, it appends a PATH line to the user's shell rc file. For fish users it targets `~/.config/fish/config.fish`, but it does **not** create the parent directory first.

On machines where `~/.config/fish/` does not exist yet, the installer fails with a "No such file or directory" write error, aborting the whole install even though the binaries were downloaded/verified correctly.

# Root Cause
`configure_path()` writes to `$config_file` without ensuring `dirname($config_file)` exists.

# Fix
- In `configure_path()` (non-dry-run path), ensure the parent directory exists before any append (e.g. `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$config_file")"`).
- Keep `--dry-run` side-effect free (do **not** create directories/files in dry-run).

# Acceptance
- `install.sh --easy-mode` succeeds for fish users on fresh machines (no pre-existing fish config dir).
- Existing behavior for bash/zsh remains unchanged.
close_reason: Completed: install.sh easy-mode now ensures the fish config directory exists before appending to ~/.config/fish/config.fish (dry-run remains side-effect free).

title: Epic: Mobile UI Hyper-Optimization
description:
Transform the mobile experience from 'functional' to 'world-class' — achieving the polish and feel of apps like Linear, Apple Notes, or Notion mobile.

## Context & Background

The current mobile implementation has solid foundations:
- ✅ Bottom navigation with safe area handling
- ✅ Touch targets at 44px minimum (WCAG compliant)
- ✅ Fluid typography with clamp() functions
- ✅ Glassmorphism effects and animations
- ✅ Dark mode support

However, 'functional' ≠ 'world-class'. This epic addresses the gap between 'works on mobile' and 'delightful on mobile'.

## User Value

**Primary users**: Researchers reviewing Brenner material on mobile devices
**Key scenarios**:
1. Quick reference lookup during meetings/commutes
2. Extended reading sessions on tablets
3. Sharing specific quotes/sections via mobile
4. Cross-referencing between distillations

## Goals

1. **Visual Polish**: Every pixel intentional, consistent spacing, refined micro-interactions
2. **Reading Experience**: Optimize for long-form content consumption on small screens
3. **Performance**: 60fps animations, no layout shifts, instant interactions
4. **Gesture Support**: Natural swipe navigation, pull-to-refresh where appropriate
5. **Accessibility**: Works perfectly with VoiceOver/TalkBack, proper contrast ratios

## Anti-Goals

- NOT building a native app (this is web optimization)
- NOT adding offline-first PWA features (separate epic if needed)
- NOT redesigning the desktop experience

## Success Metrics

- Lighthouse mobile performance score > 95
- No layout shift (CLS = 0)
- Touch interactions feel 'native'
- User feedback: 'feels like a native app'

## Technical Considerations

- Framework: Next.js 16.10 + React 19 (App Router)
- Styling: Tailwind v4 with existing design system
- Testing: Playwright for E2E, manual device testing
- Key breakpoints: sm(640), md(768), lg(1024)

## Dependencies

This epic has no external blockers but benefits from:
- Testing infrastructure for visual regression testing

title: Feature: Hypothesis Registry Schema
description:
# Feature: Hypothesis Registry Schema (ENHANCED)

## Purpose
Define the canonical data schema for tracking hypotheses across sessions. This is the foundational infrastructure that all other Research Intelligence features depend on.

## CRITICAL UPDATES from Review

After reviewing the artifact schema and evaluation rubric, the hypothesis schema needs these additions:

### Missing Fields Identified:
1. **mechanism** — HOW would this work? Not just WHAT it claims.
2. **anchors** — §n citations to transcript (provenance!)
3. **linkedAssumptions** — Which assumptions does this hypothesis depend on?
4. **linkedAnomalies** — Which anomalies does this hypothesis attempt to explain?
5. **linkedCritiques** — Active critiques targeting this hypothesis
6. **confidence** — How confident are we? (high/medium/low/speculative)
7. **category** — Type of hypothesis (mechanistic/phenomenological/boundary/auxiliary)

### Enhanced Schema

```typescript
export const HypothesisConfidenceSchema = z.enum([
  'high',        // Strong theoretical/empirical backing
  'medium',      // Reasonable but untested
  'low',         // Speculative
  'speculative', // Wild idea worth exploring
]);

export const HypothesisCategorySchema = z.enum([
  'mechanistic',      // Proposes a causal mechanism
  'phenomenological', // Describes a pattern without mechanism
  'boundary',         // Defines scope/applicability
  'auxiliary',        // Supporting hypothesis (not the main question)
  'third_alternative', // The "both could be wrong" option
]);

export const HypothesisSchema = z.object({
  /** Stable ID format: H-{session_id}-{sequence} e.g., H-RS20251230-001 */
  id: z.string().regex(/^H-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}$/),
  
  /** Human-readable claim statement */
  statement: z.string().min(10).max(500),
  
  /** HOW would this work? The causal mechanism. REQUIRED for mechanistic hypotheses. */
  mechanism: z.string().optional(),
  
  /** Source type */
  origin: z.enum(['proposed', 'third_alternative', 'refinement', 'anomaly_spawned']),
  
  /** Category of hypothesis */
  category: HypothesisCategorySchema,
  
  /** Confidence level */
  confidence: HypothesisConfidenceSchema,
  
  /** If this is a refinement/alternative, link to parent hypothesis */
  parentId: z.string().optional(),
  
  /** If spawned from an anomaly, link to the anomaly */
  spawnedFromAnomaly: z.string().optional(),  // X-xxx ID
  
  /** Session where this hypothesis was created */
  sessionId: z.string(),
  
  /** Agent that proposed this hypothesis */
  proposedBy: z.string().optional(),
  
  /** Current lifecycle state */
  state: HypothesisStateSchema,
  
  // === PROVENANCE ===
  
  /** §n transcript anchors */
  anchors: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  
  /** Is this an inference? (not directly from Brenner) */
  isInference: z.boolean().default(false),
  
  // === LINKS ===
  
  /** Which assumptions does this hypothesis depend on? */
  linkedAssumptions: z.array(z.string()).optional(),  // A-xxx IDs
  
  /** Which anomalies does this hypothesis attempt to explain? */
  linkedAnomalies: z.array(z.string()).optional(),  // X-xxx IDs
  
  /** Active critiques targeting this hypothesis (computed/cached) */
  unresolvedCritiqueCount: z.number().default(0),
  
  // === TIMESTAMPS ===
  
  createdAt: z.string().datetime(),
  updatedAt: z.string().datetime(),
  
  // === METADATA ===
  
  /** Tags for categorization */
  tags: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  
  /** Free-form notes */
  notes: z.string().optional(),
});
```

## Validation Rules

From evaluation rubric "Level Separation" (0-3):
- **mechanism** field should not conflate levels (program vs interpreter)
- Check for level conflation red flags:
  - "The gene tells the cell to..." (anthropomorphizing)
  - "The organism decides to..." (agency confusion)
  - Confusing "won't" (chastity) with "can't" (impotence)

From evaluation rubric "Third Alternative Presence" (0-3):
- Every hypothesis set MUST have a third_alternative category
- Third alternative must be "genuinely orthogonal" not just "both wrong"

## CLI Commands

- `brenner hypothesis list [--state=...] [--category=...] [--confidence=...]`
- `brenner hypothesis show <id>` — Now shows linked assumptions, anomalies, critiques
- `brenner hypothesis create --statement="..." --mechanism="..." --category=mechanistic`
- `brenner hypothesis link-assumption <hypothesis-id> <assumption-id>`
- `brenner hypothesis link-anomaly <hypothesis-id> <anomaly-id>`
- `brenner hypothesis search <query>` — Full-text across statement + mechanism

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Enhanced schema with mechanism, anchors, category, confidence
- [ ] Links to assumptions, anomalies, critiques
- [ ] Third alternative enforcement (every set must have one)
- [ ] Level separation validation (warn on conflation patterns)
- [ ] Provenance tracking (anchors, isInference)

## Related Specs
- specs/artifact_schema_v0.1.md — Section 2: Hypothesis Slate
- specs/evaluation_rubric_v0.1.md — Criteria 4, 5, 6
close_reason: Implemented comprehensive Hypothesis Registry Schema with Zod. Includes: enhanced schema with mechanism, anchors, category, confidence, linked assumptions/anomalies, provenance tracking. Added level conflation detection, third alternative validation, ID generation, factory functions, and 35 passing unit tests.

Create `/glossary` route with full searchable index of all terms, category filtering, and deep-link support.

- `/glossary` - Full glossary
- `/glossary#machine-language` - Deep link to specific term (auto-opens details)

- Title: "Glossary"
- Description: "Plain-English definitions for technical terms..."

- Category pills: All | Operators | Brenner | Biology | Bayesian | Method | Project

- Expanded: full long definition, why-we-use-it box (green accent), analogy box (primary accent), related terms with links

title: TASK: Implement Session Archival, Deletion & Storage Management
description:
## Managing Session Lifecycle

Users will accumulate sessions over time. They need to:
- Archive completed sessions
- Delete unwanted sessions
- Manage storage space
- Export before deletion

### Session States (Extended)

\`\`\`typescript
type SessionStatus = 
  | 'active'      // Currently in progress
  | 'completed'   // Finished, research brief generated
  | 'archived'    // Hidden from main view, still accessible
  | 'deleted';    // Marked for deletion (soft delete)
\`\`\`

### Archive Flow

\`\`\`
Session completed
     │
     ▼
User clicks "Archive"
     │
     ▼
Session moves to "Archived" section
     │
     ├──► Can be restored to active
     └──► Can be permanently deleted
\`\`\`

### Deletion Flow (with safeguards)

\`\`\`
User clicks "Delete"
     │
     ▼
Confirmation modal:
"This will permanently delete your session.
 Consider exporting first. This cannot be undone."
 
 [Export First] [Cancel] [Delete Forever]
     │                          │
     │                          ▼
     ▼                    Soft delete
Export modal              (30-day grace)
     │                          │
     ▼                          ▼
Download JSON/MD         Permanent deletion
\`\`\`

### Storage Management

Show storage usage:
\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Storage Usage                                                  │
│                                                                 │
│  ████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  2.3 MB / 10 MB              │
│                                                                 │
│  Sessions: 12 active, 5 archived                                │
│  Largest: "PhD Research" (450 KB)                               │
│                                                                 │
│  [Clear Archived] [Export All]                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### UI Components

Session List Actions:
\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Social Media Hypothesis                           ⋮ Menu       │
│ COMPLETED • Research brief ready                               │
│                                                                 │
│  Menu:                                                         │
│  ├─ View Session                                                │
│  ├─ Export (JSON, Markdown, PDF)                                │
│  ├─ Duplicate                                                   │
│  ├─ Archive                                                     │
│  └─ Delete                                                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### Archived Section

\`\`\`
Archived Sessions (5)  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Old Nutrition Study                              [Restore] [×]  │
│ Archived 2 months ago • 120 KB                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### Implementation Details

\`\`\`typescript
// Soft delete with grace period
interface DeletedSession {
  sessionId: string;
  deletedAt: Date;
  expiresAt: Date;  // 30 days later
  reason?: string;
}

// Storage quota management
const STORAGE_QUOTA_MB = 10;
const WARNING_THRESHOLD = 0.8;

function checkStorageQuota(): StorageStatus {
  const used = calculateStorageUsage();
  return {
    used,
    total: STORAGE_QUOTA_MB,
    percentUsed: used / STORAGE_QUOTA_MB,
    warning: used / STORAGE_QUOTA_MB > WARNING_THRESHOLD
  };
}
\`\`\`

### File Locations
\`\`\`
apps/web/src/lib/brenner-loop/storage.ts
apps/web/src/components/brenner-loop/SessionActions.tsx
apps/web/src/components/brenner-loop/StorageManager.tsx
apps/web/src/components/brenner-loop/ArchiveSection.tsx
\`\`\`

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Archive/restore sessions works
- [ ] Delete with confirmation and export option
- [ ] Storage usage displayed
- [ ] Warning when approaching quota
- [ ] Bulk actions (clear all archived)

### Depends On
- 1v26.2 (LocalStorage Persistence)
- reew.4 (Session List Page)
